title: A local property with the cancellation property is inherited by the second of two composable morphisms
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: For a local property of morphisms of complete weakly admissible rings with the cancellation property, and composable morphisms of locally countably indexed formal algebraic spaces, the lemma asserts that if the composite and the second morphism satisfy the equivalent conditions defining the property then so does the first (statement lines 5389-5397). The proof reduces to the affine case by three successive coverings -- of the target, then of the two base changes over each member -- and observes that the members obtained correspond to arrows of complete weakly admissible rings arranged as a composite (proof lines 5399-5411). Under the hypothesis, the two arrows out of the base satisfy the property, and the cancellation property then gives the property for the arrow from the middle to the source, which is what had to be shown (proof lines 5411-5415). The claim is H2: the covering reduction is explicit and the only algebraic input is the cancellation property, applied to the triangle of arrows obtained from the coverings.
